description:
# **About Realm Hack '26**

**Realm Hack '26** is the flagship annual hackathon organized by CFRA — Computer Science Forum: Realm of Academics, College of Engineering Karunagappally. 

Built for students and independent developers across India, Realm Hack brings together builders, and problem-solvers to create impactful technology solutions. The hackathon is designed as a three-round selection process, ensuring every team is evaluated on both the quality of its idea and its technical execution before the on-campus finale. 

Whether you're building your first project or your next big startup idea, Realm Hack '26 is your opportunity to learn, collaborate, and compete on a national stage.

### Hackathon Structure

**Round 1 — Registration & Idea Submission**
* Register your team on Devfolio and submit a project title, technology track, and a short abstract describing your idea.
* Applications are reviewed for originality, problem relevance, innovation, feasibility, and potential impact.
* Selected teams advance to Round 2 — Online Technical Evaluation.

**Round 2 — Online Technical Evaluation**
* Round 2 is conducted through the official Realm Hack website and is open only to teams shortlisted from Round 1.
* Shortlisted teams will receive access to the Round 2 submission portal, where they can download the official 4-slide PPT template and submit their technical proposal before the submission deadline.
* Submissions in this round are evaluated to shortlist teams for the Offline Grand Finale. 
* Teams shortlisted from Round 2 will receive an official invitation to compete in the Offline Grand Finale.

**Round 3 — Offline Grand Finale**
* Teams shortlisted from Round 2 will be invited to the Realm Hack '26 Grand Finale at the College of Engineering Karunagappally.
* Finalists will participate in a 24-hour offline hackathon, build and present their solutions before an expert judging panel, connect with mentors and industry professionals, and compete for the ₹60,000 prize pool.

### Who Can Participate?
* Students from any college or university in India.
* Individual developers and teams of 1–4 members.

### Official Website
Full rules, submission guidelines, announcements, and Round 2 updates will be available on the official website: [realmhack.in](https://realmhack.in)

hackathon_faqs.answer: Realm Hack '26 is open to students from colleges and universities across India, as well as independent developers.
hackathon_faqs.question: Who can participate?

hackathon_faqs.answer: Hybrid. Rounds 1 and 2 are fully online. Only teams selected from Round 2 attend the offline 24-hour Grand Finale on campus.
hackathon_faqs.question: Is this hackathon online or offline?

hackathon_faqs.answer: Three rounds. Round 1 is registration and idea submission on Devfolio. Shortlisted teams advance to Round 2, an online technical evaluation conducted through the Realm Hack website. Teams selected from Round 2 advance to the Offline Grand Finale.
hackathon_faqs.question: How does the selection process work?

hackathon_faqs.answer: No. Clearing Round 1 means you advance to Round 2, which is still online. Only teams selected at the end of Round 2 are invited to the Grand Finale.
hackathon_faqs.question: If I clear Round 1, am I going to the finale?

hackathon_faqs.answer: Teams submit their selected hackathon track, project title, and a short description of their proposed solution. No code or presentation is required in Round 1.
hackathon_faqs.question: What do I submit in Round 1?

hackathon_faqs.answer: A four-slide implementation proposal, submitted on the Realm Hack website. The template and submission portal open after Round 1 results are announced. Only Round 1 qualifiers receive access. Submissions with more than four slides are not evaluated.
hackathon_faqs.question: What do I submit in Round 2, and where?

hackathon_faqs.answer: Yes. The Grand Finale is a fully offline 24-hour hackathon at the College of Engineering Karunagappally, Kerala, on 23–24 October 2026. Finalist teams must be able to travel to the venue and participate in person.
hackathon_faqs.question: Do finalists have to attend in person?

hackathon_faqs.answer: Research, planning, and design are allowed. The main implementation must happen during the 24-hour finale.
hackathon_faqs.question: Can I start building before the finale?

hackathon_faqs.answer: A ₹60,000 prize pool awarded at the Grand Finale, along with sponsor credits and perks from our partners. Rounds 1 and 2 are selection rounds only.
